texts.preamble: Arnab Basu vs Bikash Chandra Chattopadhyay & Another on 18 December, 2017
texts.facts: The grievance of the petitioner is against a proceeding arising out of case no.1D of 2002 under Section 16(1)(a)(i) read with Section 7 of the Prevention of Food Adulteration Act, 1954 pending before the learned Metropolitan and Municipal Magistrate, 4th Court, Kolkata wherein process was issued against the petitioner along with two others vide order dated January 25, 2002 on the basis of a petition of complaint filed by the Food Inspector, Kolkata Municipal Corporation who is the opposite party no. 1 herein.
texts.arguments: Mr. Sen, learned counsel appearing for the petitioner submits that a complaint against the director of the company is not maintainable unless a criminal act is specified against him. It is argued that there is no allegation in the petition of complaint against this petitioner who is the Director of the company named M/s. Switz Food (P) Ltd. so the proceeding as regards this petitioner is liable to be [LEAKAGE_MASK]. To fortify his submission learned advocate for the petitioner placed reliance upon the decision reported in 1983 Supreme Court Cases (Cri) 115 in the case of Municipal Corporation of Delhi -Versus- Ram Kishan Rohtagi And Others. Reference has also been made to a decision of Punjab and Haryana High Court in the case of Subhash Chand @ Subhash K. Aggarwal - Versus- State (Chandigarh Administration), Chandigarh, reported in 2011(2) FAC 107. The case of L. N. Bangur & Others -Versus- The Food Inspector & Another, reported in (2011)2 FAC 340 of Kerala High Court and Gauhati High Court's decision in the case of Shri Dulal Mandal & Others -Versus- The State of Assam, reported in 2011(2) FAC 355 have also been referred. Learned advocate appearing for the opposite party no. 1 countered by inviting the attention of this Court to the provisions of Section 17(1)(a)(ii) of the Prevention of Food Adulteration Act, 1954 and argued that in view of the aforesaid provision the petitioner being the Director of the company cannot shirk his responsibility for the conduct of the business of the company. In this context it would be profitable to refer to the relevant provisions of Section 17(1) of the Act which provides as follows : Arnab Basu vs Bikash Chandra Chattopadhyay & Another on 18 December, 2017 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/167329926/ 1 "17. Offences by companies. - (1) Where an offence under this Act has been committed by a company - (a) (i) the person, if any, who has been nominated under sub-section (2) to be in charge of, and responsible to, the company for the conduct of the business of the company (hereafter in this section referred to as the person responsible), or (ii) where no person has been so nominated, every person who at the time the offence was committed was in charge of, and was responsible to, the company for the conduct of the business of the company; and (b) the company, shall be deemed to be guilty of the offence and shall be liable to be proceeded against and punished accordingly: Provided that nothing contained in this sub-section shall render any such person liable to any punishment provided in this Act if he proves that the offence was committed without his knowledge and that he exercised all due diligence to prevent the commission of such offence." Curiously enough, there is no averment in the petition of complaint that the petitioner whose name figures therein as the accused no. 2 - Director of M/s. Switz Food (P) Ltd. was in charge of and was responsible to the company for the conduct of the business of the said company.
